summary: In Ramadan of 8 AH, the Prophet ﷺ marched on Makkah with an army of 10,000 and entered the city with virtually no bloodshed. He declared a general amnesty for the Quraysh, smashed the 360 idols in and around the Kaabah, and delivered a khutbah establishing that all people are equal before Allah. It was the defining triumph of the prophetic mission.
narrative:
The immediate trigger for the conquest was the violation of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah by the Quraysh's allies, the Banu Bakr, who attacked the Banu Khuza'ah — allies of the Muslims — killing a number of them near Makkah while Quraysh fighters participated. When news reached the Prophet ﷺ, he began preparations for a major campaign while keeping the destination secret.

Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, having heard rumours of a coming Muslim force, rode to Madinah to seek a renewal of the treaty. He spoke first with his daughter Umm Habibah ؓ — who had become the Prophet's wife — then with Abu Bakr ؓ, Umar ؓ, and finally with the Prophet ﷺ himself, all of whom offered him no reassurance. He returned to Makkah uncertain. Al-Tabari records that Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib ؓ encountered Abu Sufyan on the road before he left and brought him back to the Prophet ﷺ on the night the Muslim army was setting out. He guided Abu Sufyan through the Muslim camp so he could see the scale of the force — fire after fire, regiment after regiment — and in the morning, at Abbas's urging, Abu Sufyan accepted Islam before the Prophet ﷺ.

The army — 10,000 strong, the largest the Prophet ﷺ had led — approached Makkah in four columns from different directions, commanded by Khalid ibn al-Walid ؓ, Zubayr ibn al-Awwam ؓ, Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah ؓ, and Sad ibn Ubadah ؓ. The Prophet ﷺ ordered that no blood be shed except in the case of those who drew swords or those who had been specifically condemned for grave crimes.

Ibn Hisham records that Khalid's column encountered brief resistance near the pass of Khandamah from Quraysh fighters who had refused the order to stand down, and a few were killed in this skirmish. Otherwise, the city was entered with almost no bloodshed. The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah on his camel, his head bowed in humility, reciting Surah al-Fath — 'Indeed We have given you a clear conquest.'

Upon reaching the Masjid al-Haram, the Prophet ﷺ performed tawaf of the Kaabah while mounted, then dismounted and entered it. He found 360 idols arranged around and inside the Kaabah. With his staff he struck each one, reciting: 'Truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish' (17:81). Bilal ibn Rabah ؓ called the adhan from atop the Kaabah itself — perhaps the most symbolic moment of the conquest, the freed African slave calling the prayer over the city that had once enslaved him.

The Prophet ﷺ then stood at the door of the Kaabah and addressed the assembled Quraysh, who awaited their fate having submitted and gathered. Ibn Hisham preserves his words: 'O Quraysh, what do you think I will do with you?' They replied: 'Good — you are a generous brother and the son of a generous brother.' He ﷺ said: 'I say to you as Yusuf said to his brothers: No blame upon you today. Go, for you are free.' This general amnesty was extended to all, with a small number of exceptions — individuals condemned for specific crimes, including the killing of Muslims and apostasy after Islam. Most of even these were eventually pardoned when they came forward with sincerity.

Al-Tabari records that among those given individual amnesty was Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, who fled to sea but whose wife caught up with him; Hind bint Utbah, the wife of Abu Sufyan, who had mutilated Hamzah ؓ at Uhud; and the singer Abdallah ibn Khatal, who was not pardoned and was killed. Wahshi ibn Harb, who had killed Hamzah ؓ, presented himself and the Prophet ﷺ forgave him, asking only that he stay out of his sight.

The conquest of Makkah was a watershed. Within days, delegations from surrounding tribes began arriving in Madinah to accept Islam, setting in motion what became known as the Year of Delegations.
